title: Y1DA--REPLACE ROOFS AND REPAIR FACADES BUILDING 6 AND 7 AT THE NORTHPORT VA MEDICAL CENTER PROJECT NUMBER: 632-23-112
description: ****** THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY ****** This is a public synopsis of a forthcoming solicitation in accordance with FAR 36.213-2. This is NOT a solicitation, and no solicitation documents are currently publicly available. This pre-solicitation notice is for Solicitation Number 36C24226B0059, Project Number 632-23-112, for the Replace Roofs and Repair Facades Buildings 6 and 7 at the Northport VA Medical Center located on 79 Middleville Road, Northport, NY 11768. This project will be 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Set-Aside (SDVOSB). Competition for this procurement is restricted to verified SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (SDVOSB) Contractors. The SDVOSB must be a small business under the relevant NAICS code and must be registered and verified in SBA's Small Business Search (https://search.certifications.sba.gov/) and https://www.sam.gov. The NAICS code for this procurement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, size standard: $45 million. IAW VAAR 852.219-10, the VIP-listed SDVOSB. Prospective Contractor will not pay more than 85% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to firms that are not VIP-listed SDVOSBs. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. SCOPE OF WORK: The Scope of Work shall generally consist of, but not limited to the following: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), NCO 2, Northport VA Medical Center, is seeking highly qualified construction firms to perform full roof replacement and repair of historical brick and stone facades at Building 6 and Building 7. Building 6 is fully occupied, and work will be phased in four stages to limit impact to one side of the building at a time. Building 7 is mostly vacant except for the basement level, and work can be completed in a single phase while maintaining protected exit access from the basement. The project includes complete roof replacement at both buildings, including flashing, fascia boards and trim, soffits, drip edges, underlayment, and shingles, along with replacement of deteriorated roof sheathing where required. Facade work includes repair of distressed brick masonry (cracking, spalling, bowing, and mortar deterioration), repointing to match existing mortar, replacement of damaged cast stone water table sections and windowsills, and stripping, cleaning, and refinishing or replacing window lintel support angles. Additional work includes reconstruction of the main entrance stair and support walls at Building 7, replacement of storm drainage and site drainage systems including new yard drains, catch basins, and underground piping with associated regrading and landscape restoration, and abatement of asbestos-containing materials as indicated on the drawings. PROJECT COMPLETION: Contractor to start immediately after receiving the Notice to Proceed and complete required work in 400 calendar days. Prospective contractors must be registered at https://www.sam.gov in accordance with 38 CFR Part 74 and VAAR 819.70 to be eligible for award. There will be a site visit held for this project and all prospective bidders are strongly encouraged to attend. Details of the site visit will be included in the solicitation document. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be issued on/about September 25, 2026. Information for Bid details, Specifications, Drawings and Contract Forms will be available in electronic format only at: https://www.sam.gov. All interested parties (subs & primes) should register for a user account which lets you save searches, follow changes to opportunities, and join interested vendor lists, and verified as a SDVOSB in SBA's Small Business Search (https://search.certifications.sba.gov/) at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. To preserve the integrity of the procurement process, all questions must be submitted in writing to Yingjie Yeung, Contract Specialist, via email at Yingjie.yeung@va.gov. End of Description

title: Collection of surface water samples and ancillary data for the Canadian Water Monitoring Program for Pesticides in priority Ontario watersheds.
description: Health Canada (HC) evaluates the risks to human health and the environment associated with the use of pesticides and regulates pesticide products in Canada under the Pest Control Products Act. In the interest of increasing the availability of real-world data for use in pesticide risk assessments, HC coordinates the Canadian Water Monitoring Program for Pesticides (CWMPP). As part of this program, water samples are analysed to determine the concentrations of pesticides present in Canadian waters. Federal laboratories will analyse approximately 200 chemicals (i.e., pesticide active ingredients and transformation products) in water from various regions across Canada. Ancillary data and expert advice assist in improving our collective understanding of any patterns observed or any potential levels of concern.

title: Purchase of eleven (11) Electrometer/High-Resistance Meters and Accessories (Keithley 6517B or Equivalent)
description: The National Research Council Canada (NRC) requires to purchase eleven (11) Electrometer/High-Resistance Meters and Accessories (Keithley 6517B, or equivalent). The equipment is used continuously in applications where low-current and high-resistance measurements require exceptional signal-to-noise performance, stability, leakage control, guarding, triaxial connectivity, and measurement repeatability. METRO operates under a rigorous quality system and maintains measurement standards that must be demonstrably traceable, reliable, and internationally recognized. The existing Keithley-based measurement platform has been fully integrated into validated measurement systems, software applications, automation scripts, operating procedures, and technical documentation. Maintaining the same instrument platform supports compatibility with internationally accepted metrology practices and helps ensure continuity and comparability of measurement results used to support national measurement standards and regulatory obligations. The use of an equivalent manufacturer's instrument would require extensive technical evaluation and verification before it could be incorporated into operational measurement systems. This work would include performance testing, comparison studies, revalidation of measurement methods, review and potential revisions, updates to quality-system documentation, modifications to software drivers and automation scripts, and assessment of impacts on established laboratory procedures. In addition, evaluation of a competing instrument would likely require acquisition of a demonstration unit and could result in disruptions to ongoing operations, delays to standards-maintenance activities, and potential interruptions to services provided to clients.

title: ACAN-NRCan Nuvis Techonologies Inc. Support
description: The Petawawa Research Forest (PRF) is a 10,000-hectare (ha) research forest located in Chalk River, Ontario. The land, which the PRF is on, is owned by the Canadian Department of National Defence (DND), Garrison Petawawa, however, under a joint memorandum of understanding (MOU) the PRF is staffed and operated by Natural Resources Canada (NRCan). Under this MOU, NRCan is responsible for wildfire detection for the entire property, approximately 30,000 ha’s. To date, fire detection on the property has been conducted using two fire towers with cupola’s (27.5 and 38.5 metres tall) staffed with personnel who visually detect fires/smoke and biangulate the location. In 2018, the 38.5-METRE-TALL tower was decommissioned limiting our ability to detect fire on the property. There is also a radio tower located on PRF property. This tower, referred to as the “Radio Tower”, has not been used for fire detection in the past. However, this tower has electrical power, which supplies power to the radio repeater that is currently on the Radio Tower. The Radio Tower can have more than one piece of equipment attached to its structure (i.e. the radio repeater will remain on the Radio Tower) and is a suitable location for a fire detection camera. NRCan was able to replace the existing fire detection system in 2022 by way of installing two optical camera sensor systems with fire detection monitoring software by Nuvis Technologies Inc. The objective of this requirement is to renew hardware and software support for the existing wildfire camera detection system. The work will involve the following: Support for Wildfire Guardian Software: 1. Support and maintenance of the existing software environment 2. Diagnostics and troubleshooting of bugs or software issues 3. Administrator support 4. Software upgrades as they are available Hardware Support for all equipment: 1. annual preventative maintenance; 2. seasonal startup and shutdown; and 3. corrective maintenance labour.

title: Industry Day - Selma AL Flood Management Risk and Bank
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile District, will conduct an industry day to discuss the design and construction of a flood risk management and bank stabilization project near downtown Selma, Alabama. The current design is anticipated to consist of approximately 1,000 linear feet of soldier-pile wall along the Alabama River. The soldier pile wall would be constructed to a top elevation of 100-ft NAVD88, and a secondary retaining wall would be constructed to a top elevation of 110-ft NAVD88. Rip-rap protection would be placed at the toe of the wall to a top elevation of 90-ft NAVD88. The event is scheduled from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. CDT on Thursday, October 28, 2026, at the Mobile District Annex Building, 201 Saint Michael St, Mobile, AL 36602.

description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform to support the procurement of spare battery carriers for Detector Special Purpose (DSP) 27. There is a requirement for a stock of spare battery carriers for Detector Special Purpose (DSP) 27. There is no other equipment which can be used in place of DSP 27. DSP 27 was brought in as a UOR, made by DSTL and Gill Research and Development Ltd, who now own the IPR and Manufacturers Data Pack. DSP 27 is a hand carried detector unit that consists of a lower 'Passive' receiving antenna head, main body, carry handle / control panel, battery carrier and upper receiving antenna. Purchase of x100 battery carriers to prevent a capability gap. This is a procurement of a spare part only. The battery carrier must be NSN 6160-99-667-2326. Milestones are not expected - immediate purchase will be the only output. Upon delivery, a short inspection of each item will be undertaken to ensure it is the correct part as expected. Success here will be seen as acceptance. OEM owns the IPR. Government Furnished Supplies Not required. Approach A pre-existing option already exists, developed by the OEM (who own the IPR and Technical Data Pack) and is deemed appropriate by the Requirements Manager. Payment One off payment paid on delivery. Contract Management Arrangements No ongoing contract. End of Contract/Exit Strategy Not applicable. Final Reminders This item already exists and is in-service. NSN 6160-99-667-2326. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. Contact Information For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title TSS 807 Opportunity

title: Maintenance Compound Electrical Distribution, Riding Mountain National Park
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to provide all labour, materials, equipment, supervision, and related services necessary to construct a new electrical distribution system at the Riding Mountain National Park Maintenance Compound in Wasagaming, Manitoba. The project involves the installation of underground conduits and electrical distribution lines, completion of all required electrical connections, and implementation of the electrical distribution design that will service all buildings from a new Customer Service Termination Enclosure (CSTE) being installed as part of Manitoba Hydro’s redevelopment of the compound’s electrical infrastructure. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE The Contractor must perform and complete the Work by March 15, 2027. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT There will be a site visit on Wednesday, October 21, 2026 at 11:00 am (MDT). Interested bidders are to meet at the Maintenance Compound (1 Compound Road, Onanole, Manitoba). Bidders are requested to communicate with the Contracting Authority before the optional site visit to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders may be requested to sign an attendance sheet. Bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative will not be given an alternative appointment but they will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE -NONCOMPETITIVE- TRANE® Building Automation System (BAS) and Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) (BAS HVAC) Control System Inspection, Maintenance, Upgrades, and Repair The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 19, intends to award a sole source contract to a single source, R.L. Armacost, Inc. for Control System Inspection, Maintenance, Upgrades, and Repair and for parts and services for the TRANE® Tracer Summit Automation System (Tracer) and TRANE® Tracer System Controller (SC) systems. Services shall include Control System Services, Integration services, system upgrade, inspection, parts repair and/or replacement, and maintenance for the Sheridan VA Healthcare System (SVAMC) at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, WY 82801. NAICS Code: 238220 Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million The TRANE ® systems control various electric, electronic, and mechanical integrating different types of building systems together into one centralized location, primarily to control heating, ventilation, and air conditioning throughout the SVAHCS. TRANE® Tracer Summit Automation System (Tracer) and TRANE® Tracer System Controller (SC), firmware, software, and source code are proprietary to TRANE® and services must be performed by a certified and trained technician using specialized tools. Upgrade services will include replacement of AHU controls and associated VAV controls to replace outdated LonTalk/pneumatic and legacy TRANE® Summit controls, with Direct Digital Control (DDC) and as described in -draft- Attachment A - Statement of Work. The SVAHCS campus HVAC infrastructure consists of the following equipment, all of which is integrated into and controlled by the TRANE® Tracer Summit Building Automation System (BAS) and TRANE® Tracer SC proprietary control platform: Approximately forty-nine (49) TRANE® Air Handling Units (AHUs) Twenty-two (22) TRANE® chillers Associated campus-wide Direct Digital Control (DDC) building automation controls, sensors, and network infrastructure Services required include but are not limited to: Preventive Maintenance (PM) & inspections Software support, programming, and system configuration of the TRANE® Tracer Summit BAS and TRANE® Tracer SC platform Emergency and corrective repairs Replacement parts and labor System upgrades as required Specialized tools required are: The Rover used for Tracer Summit. Tracer TU used on the Tracer SC. PROPRIETARY SYSTEM REQUIREMENT: The TRANE® Tracer Summit BAS and TRANE® Tracer SC are proprietary software and hardware platforms. Servicing, programming, configuring, and maintaining these systems requires manufacturer-level software licensing, proprietary diagnostic tools, and TRANE®-certified technician credentials. Interested parties must demonstrate in their response that they possess the required TRANE® certifications, proprietary software access, and licensing necessary to service the existing TRANE® Tracer Summit and TRANE® Tracer SC infrastructure without requiring replacement of the existing campus control system. To ensure continuity of service and to minimize risk of operational disruption to the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the contractor must be capable of providing the complete range of services identified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The ability to perform all required maintenance, inspection, upgrades, repair, and support services without interruption is essential to maintaining operational readiness and minimizing the risk of equipment downtime. Any transition to a contractor unable to provide the full scope of services could negatively impact facility operations and patient care. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: February 1, 2027 January 31, 2030, with a base year and two 1-year ordering periods. NOTICE OF INTENT: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement along with the information requested below, which shall be considered by the Government. The Government will consider responses received by the closing date of this notice. The proprietary nature of this requirement has been verified with an intent to sole source with no responses. Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1. If the Government decides to compete this requirement, a synopsis shall be issued utilizing the combined synopsis/solicitation procedure identified in FAR 12.603. REQUESTED INFORMATION: Interested parties capable of providing the described services are invited to submit a written capabilities statement that includes the following information: Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), HUBZone, 8(a), etc.). If claiming SDVOSB or VOSB status, provide your SBA certification number as verified through the Small Business Search (SBS) website at https://search.certifications.sba.gov. Current TRANE® manufacturer certifications held by your firm and/or technicians, specifically for the TRANE® Tracer Summit BAS and TRANE® Tracer SC platforms. Documentation or description of your firm's current authorized access to TRANE® proprietary software, diagnostic tools, and licensing required to service the TRANE® Tracer Summit and TRANE® Tracer SC systems. A narrative describing your firm's experience performing similar HVAC and BAS maintenance services on TRANE® Tracer Summit and/or TRANE® Tracer SC systems, including contract references (contract number, agency/customer name, point of contact, telephone number, period of performance, and dollar value). Your firm's SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number and confirmation of active SAM.gov registration. However, if a firm believes it can meet the requirements it must furnish a capability statement and supporting evidence/information about its products, services, and certified technicians, as well as authorization from the OEM to provide service to the Contract Specialist by the date and time listed below. All interested and capable firms are encouraged to respond regardless of business size. Responses must be submitted via email to: Christine Jarvis, Christine.jarvis@va.gov no later than OCTOBER 28, 2026 at 10:00 AM Mountain Time. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: Military Uniform Alterations and Tailoring Services 1. This notice is issued to determine interest, capability, and the availability of qualified commercial vendors (specifically small businesses) to support regional military tailoring requirements. 2. Purpose and Objective The USPFO for Illinois is conducting market research to identify qualified commercial vendors capable of performing high-quality military uniform alterations and insignia attachment services. Services will support Traditional Drilling (M-Day) enlisted Soldiers and authorized Active Guard Reserve (AGR) personnel across various state readiness centers/armories. The Government intends to analyze responses to determine whether to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for continuous regional needs, a firm-fixed-price Commercial Service Contract for large-scale unit events, or handle low-volume requests via Government Purchase Card (GPC) micro-purchases. 3. Scope of Work (SOW) Contractors will be required to provide precise custom tailoring, fitting, and sewing modifications. All work must strictly comply with Army Regulation (AR) 670-1 (Wear and Appearance of Army Uniforms) and AR 700-84 (Tables 13-1 and 13-2). Authorized services span across the following uniform items: Army Green Service Uniform (AGSU) Coats: Shortening/lengthening sleeves, adjusting hemlines, taking in/letting out shoulders, collars, back waist lengths, side/back seams, front button realignment, female bust alterations, and sewing sleeve ornamental/soutache braids. AGSU Trousers, Slacks, & Skirts: Adjusting waists, seats, and crotches; adding fabric or completing bottom hemming; attaching leg braids or blood stripes. Service Shirts (Heritage Tan 521): Altering side/back seams; shortening sleeves (if excess exceeds 1 inch) and resetting cuff buttons. Operational Camouflage Pattern (OCP / IHWCU) Uniforms: Tailoring is strictly limited to shortening trouser lengths. No other modifications are authorized. Accoutrements & Insignia Placement: Direct sew-on attachment of enlisted sleeve rank chevrons, shoulder sleeve unit patches, branch tapes, name tapes, combat badges, service stripes, and overseas bars; safe removal of old patches. 4. Brick-and-Mortar Regional Support: Operating a physical commercial tailoring facility within reasonable geographic proximity to Illinois National Guard hub locations to accept individual authorized Soldiers carrying official work orders (such as DA Form 3078). 6. Submission Instructions & Capability Statement Requirements Interested vendors who meet the requirements are requested to submit a concise Capability Statement (not exceeding 5 pages) detailing the following: Company Profile: Business Name, Address, Point of Contact, Phone, Email, UEI Number, and CAGE Code. title: Idaho Panhandle National Forest UTV and Track Set Purchase
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The U.S. Forest Service (USFS), Idaho Panhandle National Forests, has a requirement for the procurement and delivery of one (1) Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) and one (1) compatible all-season track kit. The equipment will be utilized by the Fire/Fuels program for wildland fire suppression and prescribed fire operations over severe, uneven terrain. All equipment must be delivered new, fully assembled, fluids serviced, and in a 100% turnkey state ready for immediate field deployment upon arrival. Note: The UTV does not have to arrive with the track set physically installed on the vehicle. However, the vehicle must be fully prepped and the track kit must arrive brand new, complete, and ready to be installed by a certified dealer To be considered responsive, contractors must submit combined pricing for both line items below: CLIN 0001: Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) Quantity: 1 EA Delivery Location: IDAHO PANHANDLE NATIONAL FORESTS SUPERVISORS OFFICE 3232 WEST NURSERY ROAD COEUR D'ALENE ID 83815 CLIN 0002: All-Season Track Kit Quantity: 1 EA Specifications: Must be 100% factory-compatible, field-interchangeable, and align directly with the vehicle awarded under CLIN 0001. Salient Characteristics (Minimum Technical Specifications) Proposed vehicles must meet or exceed the following design limits and features: Engine & Cooling: 4-stroke, liquid-cooled engine. Cylinder Displacement: Min: 998 cc | Max: 1500 cc. Horsepower: Min: 80 hp | Max: 150 hp. Dimensions: Length (120�138 in), Width (63�66 in), Height (76�82 in). Ground Clearance: Min: 13 in | Max: 20 in. Capacities: Person Capacity (2�3), Payload (1000�1700 lbs), Box Capacity (1000�1500 lbs), Towing Capacity (2500�3500 lbs). Tires: 8 to 10 ply; Size Min: 27 x 9 x 14 | Max: 30 x 11 x 15. Included Accessories/Features: Enclosed cab with full doors, hard top roof, glass full tip-out windshield with wipers, sliding window rear panel, heater/defroster, protection headache rack, front/rear a-arm protectors, skid plate, front/rear bumpers, fender flares, rock sliders, chainsaw mount, LED light bar, rearview mirror, and a >4,500 lb winch. Track Specs: Rubber tracks with a steel frame designed for all-season flotation/traction. Minimum 2-year warranty on tracks; minimum 1-year warranty on the UTV. Origin: Must be manufactured in the U.S. Delivery & Shipping Terms Delivery Timeline: All items must be physically delivered within 90 calendar days from the formal date of award. Shipping: FOB Destination. Pricing must be fully inclusive of all freight, handling, and delivery charges. The contractor is responsible for offloading equipment at the specified facility. No loading dock or equipment available to unload. UTV does not have to arrive with tracks installed but kit must be ready to be installed by a certified Evaluation and Basis for Award The Government will conduct a Side-by-Side Comparative Evaluation of quotes in accordance with simplified commercial procedures (FAR 12.201-1 and 12.205(c)(2)). Formal scoring matrices will not be used. A single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract will be awarded based on the following factors: Technical Capability & Salient Characteristics: Degree to which the solution meets or exceeds design limits and accessory bundles. Delivery Timeline: Preference/favorable evaluation may be given to shorter delivery timelines than the mandatory 90 days. Price: Evaluated to ensure fairness and reasonableness. Submission Requirements Interested vendors must have an Active Registration in SAM (https://sam.gov) at the time of quote submission. Omitting a Unique Entity ID (UEI) will exclude the quotation package from consideration. Quotation packages must be organized in the following order and submitted via email to mindy.hickman@usda.gov: Failure to provide these documents will result in your offer being exluded from concideration. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items to a single provider.

title: Sewage Ejector and Line Assessment
description: This scope of work requires the contractor to locate, inspect, and modify an unmapped 700 to 800 foot concrete-encased four inch cast iron sewer line and its associated distribution box, with mandatory Government presence during all site inspections. Key tasks include installing concrete-encased Schedule 40 PVC double-Y clean-outs every 300 feet, exposing and inspecting the distribution box and its 2009 leach field connections, and extending the box cover using a riser and structural cover rated for three ton vehicle traffic protected by four concrete-encased steel safety-yellow bollards. All physical, material, and dimensional adjustments must be documented as Red Line As-Builts on the reference drawing, and any recommended corrective actions for the lateral lines must be delivered via a detailed findings report with comprehensive labor and material cost estimates.

If you have already sent your RFIs to the POCs you do not have to resubmit them. 4 August 2026: Please see the attached RFP (FA8137-26-R-0040) and all attachments. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- THIS POSTING WILL SATISFY THE REQUIREMENT OF RFO 5.101, Presolicitation Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) for General Construction Services will accomplish a broad range of sustainment, maintenance, repair, alteration/renovation, and minor construction projects affecting real property facilities at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. title: Residential Reentry Center (RRC) and Home Confinement Services located within Sacramento County and other border counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility.
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes Residential Reentry Center Services located within Sacramento County and other border Counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four one-year options periods. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 16 beds in which 14 beds will be designated for males and 2 beds designated for females and an estimated maximum 40 bed facility in which 34 beds will be designated for males and 6 beds designated for females. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 8 placements and an estimated maximum 20 placements to include both male and female. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000019 will be available on or about October 28, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. title: C-208/PC-12 Special Missions Aircrew & Maintenance Training
description: 1. Title: Request for Information (RFI): Foreign Military Sales � C208/PC12 Aircraft Training Services and Related Training Support Services 2. Purpose: The Air Force Installation Contracting Center (AFICC) 338th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (ESS) is conducting market research for the Air Education and Training Command (AETC) Air Force Security Assistance Training (AFSAT) Squadron to identify capable commercial sources that may be able to provide aircraft training and support services for the Cessna 208B Caravan EX (C208) aircraft with Garmin 1000 avionics and Pilatus PC-12 NG aircraft with Honeywell Primus Apex. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 611512 � Flight Training, Small Business Administration (SBA) Small Business Size Standard is $34M. AFSAT seeks information to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry capability, capacity, experience, training methods, facilities, simulators or training devices, instructor qualifications, maintenance-training capabilities, and other related services supporting aircrew and maintenance personnel for the C-208/PC-12 platforms. The information requested by this RFI is for market research only and will be used by the Air Force Multi-Functional Team (MFT) to assist in acquisition planning for potential future requirements. Responses to this RFI will be used for planning and market-research purposes only. 3. Background: AFSAT has a potential requirement for contractor-provided training support associated with C-208 and PC-12 aircraft operations and sustainment. The anticipated support may include initial, recurrent, mission-specific, maintenance, and other aircraft-related training for Government personnel and International Military Students (IMS). The Department of War (DOW) training venues do not have existing capacity to support the additional requirement of Cessna 208 Mission Pilot, Mission Systems Operator (MSO) and Load Master (LM) training, in the Airland/Airdrop/ISR/ Night Vision Goggle (NVG) mission sets and Pilatus PC-12 Mission Pilot, MSO and LM training, in the Airland/Airdrop/ISR/NVG mission sets. The Government is interested in identifying sources capable of supporting training at contractor facilities, Government facilities, or other mutually agreed locations internationally, as applicable. 3. Potential Scope of Training Support AETC/A3F and AFSAT are tasked with providing pilot, Mission Systems Operator (MSO) and Loadmaster (LM) training services for its government personnel and international partners. Due to the nature and extent of personnel that require training throughout the USA and internationally, the required Contractor support services include flying training to meet the needs of the Air Force (AF) mission and the flying training requirements of our international partners. The Contractor shall obtain aircraft for use in training, maintenance of the aircraft and/or related equipment while in CONUS (OCONUS will require Contracted Logistics Support (CLS)), aircrew instructors, and student documentation for certification of pilots at the end of the training. None of the training includes combat missions or services that are intended to determine pilot requirements for readiness by the AF and AFSAT. The AF and AFSAT will utilize the Cessna 208B EX Garmin 1000 aircraft and Pilatus PC-12 Honeywell Primus APEX. The AF mission will extend over to aircrew international military operations where support for foreign language assistance is needed (interpreters as required). Currency training is also an on-going need as students are at various levels or phases of pilot experience. This educational element will require continuous learning certification to maintain aircrew flying currency and proficiency for USG and international personnel respectively. Interested vendors shall describe their ability to provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, non-personal services, and other items necessary to perform aircrew, maintenance, and training services for Cessna 208/Pilatus PC-12 platforms. Training includes: Mission Pilot, MSO and LM in the Airland/Airdrop/ISR/NVG mission sets and could include some or all of the following services: 3.1 Aircrew Training Support Services Potential aircrew training may include: Initial and recurrent pilot training. Ground school instruction. Aircraft systems training. Normal, abnormal, emergency, and emergency-procedure training. Flight training and proficiency events. Instrument Flight rules (IFR) training, as applicable. Crew Resource Management (CRM) or equivalent crew-coordination training. Mission-oriented training tailored to Government operational requirements, if applicable. Instructor pilot and standardization support. Check airman or evaluation support, if applicable and authorized. Training records administration and student performance tracking. Computer-based training, distributed learning, and instructor-led classroom instruction. 3.2 Aircraft Maintenance Training Support Services Potential maintenance training may include: Initial and recurrent maintenance technician training. Airframe, powerplant, avionics, electrical, and aircraft systems training. Troubleshooting, fault isolation, inspection, servicing, repair, and replacement procedures. Engine maintenance training, including applicable manufacturer-supported maintenance practices. Propeller, landing gear, environmental, fuel, hydraulic, electrical, and avionics-system instruction, as applicable. Maintenance documentation, technical data, parts support, and maintenance-record training. Maintenance human factors and safety training. Train-the-trainer or instructor development programs. Specialized training for field-level, intermediate-level, or organizational-level maintenance personnel, as applicable. 3.3 Additional Training and Support Services Interested vendors should also identify their capability to provide: Flight training devices (FTDs), full-flight simulators, fixed-base simulators, or other training devices. Simulator-based emergency-procedure and instrument training. Aircraft-specific courseware development, revision, and sustainment. Training needs analysis and curriculum development. Mobile training teams (MTTs). On-site or deployed training support. Training program management and scheduling. Student training records, certificates, and completion documentation. Training program quality assurance and continuous-improvement processes. Training facility support, classrooms, briefing rooms, and equipment. Training materials, technical publications, and student handouts. Training support for avionics upgrades, aircraft modifications, or mission equipment, if applicable. Ability to provide housing and ground transportation for international students Other related training services not listed above. 4. Requested Vendor Information Interested sources are requested to provide the following information: 4.1 Company Information Company name. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), if applicable. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, if applicable. Business address. Primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address. Company website. Business size and socioeconomic status, if applicable. Relevant certifications, approvals, licenses, and authorizations. 4.2 Relevant Experience Provide a summary of experience delivering training for: Cessna 208-series aircraft, including the 208B Caravan EX, if applicable. Pilatus PC-12 aircraft, including applicable variants. Comparable single-engine turboprop aircraft, if direct C-208 or PC-12 experience is limited. Government, military, law-enforcement, commercial, or international customers, as appropriate. For each relevant effort, provide: Customer type or organization, if releasable. Period of performance. Aircraft platform supported. Nature and approximate scale of training provided. Types of personnel trained. Tr

description: Area of Interest (AOI) #02: Data Exchange Services Operations, Modernization, and Development PAE DMS is interested in solutions that satisfy the Government�s need for Data Exchange Services operations, modernization, and development in support of the Enterprise Information and Data Solutions (EIDS) Program Management Office (PMO). The DHA Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Defense Medical Solutions (PAE DMS), EIDS PMO, seeks commercial solutions to support Data Exchange Platform (DxP) operations, sustainment, modernization, and development. The DxP supports mission-essential MHS Information Platform (MIP) functions by processing real-time clinical and operational data exchanged with more than 15 external systems and partners. It enables secure, standards-based interoperability among DHA, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and other Federal healthcare partners in support of military health readiness and patient-care delivery. The Government seeks commercial solutions that sustain reliable, secure, and continuously available legacy services while modernizing the platform toward scalable, cloud-native, API-driven, standards-based, and AI/ML-ready capabilities. Solutions may be commercially available or capable of configuration, integration, testing, demonstration, or modification to meet Government objectives. The Government will not consider late submissions. Vendors must submit technical and administrative questions to Lacey Lockard at lacey.n.lockard.civ@health.mil no later than 14 October 2026, 1400 Eastern Time. As appropriate, the Government may post responses to questions or otherwise provide clarifications to all potential vendors. Per the CSO terms, the Government is not liable for costs associated with preparing materials submitted in response to this AOI. Interested parties are strongly encouraged to review all attached documents in their entirety for complete information regarding this opportunity, including submission requirements and other specific instructions.

title: US Government Seeks to Lease Office Space around Hanscom AFB
description: 1. DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought notice only. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. 2. PURPOSE The United States Air Force is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing leased, off-base commercial office space in a 10-mile radius of Hanscom AFB, MA, 01731 3. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS To be considered, the proposed space must meet the following minimum parameters: Space Type: Classification Feasibility: Explicitly state what classification levels the space can support today (e.g., Unclassified, Secret/Collateral, TS/SCI, JWICS) and what upgrades would be required to meet higher levels. If no current classification levels exist, is there an ability to add them? Would upgrades remain in place once contract ends? The Government is assessing the full spectrum of security capabilities available in the local market. Please feel free to respond with what you currently have to offer, even if your facility does not meet all preferred security thresholds. For example, if you possess functional Unclassified administrative space and Secret-level secure space, but lack active JWICS (Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System) capabilities, we still strongly encourage you to submit a response. The Government is highly interested in reviewing partial, mixed, or upgradeable space configurations to determine how they might support our broader mission requirements. Space Outfitting & Furnishing Status: To assist the Government in assessing transition timelines and potential cost savings, please address the following regarding the proposed space: Existing Inventory: Indicate whether the proposed space is currently unfurnished or contains existing, usable furniture (e.g., modular cubicles, desks, conference tables) that can be utilized to reduce lead times. Installation Capabilities: Specify if the management company offers turnkey installation services for government-furnished or custom-designed cubicles, including any associated fee structures. Capacity: Must accommodate between eighty (80) and one hundred (100) personnel. Square Footage (ABOA): A minimum of 11,200 square feet up to a maximum of approximately 21,000 square feet of American National Standards Institute (ANSI)/ Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) Office Area (ABOA). Offers falling within this range that optimize spatial efficiency and allow for potential growth up to the maximum personnel count are highly encouraged Conference and Collaborative Space: Primary Requirement: At least one (1) dedicated conference or collaborative room capable of comfortably seating a minimum of twenty-five (25) personnel. The minimum size for this primary meeting space is 500 square feet. Preferred Option: The availability of secondary conference rooms, huddle spaces, or break-out areas within the offered space is highly desirable to support flexible mission workflows and concurrent meetings. Connectivity: Space must be capable of supporting standard commercial internet/ WiFi service installation. Parking: How many parking spaces are available? Covered garage parking is a �nice to have" Location: Must be located within a 10-mile radius of Hanscom AFB Occupancy and Lease Term The Government is seeking a lease structure consisting of a one-year base period with four consecutive one-year option periods, targeted for occupancy in early 2027. Contract Period | Estimated Duration | Target Timeline / Effective Dates Base Period | 12 Months | April 1, 2027 � March 31, 2028 Option Period 1 | 12 Months | April 1, 2028 � March 31, 2029 Option Period 2 | 12 Months | April 1, 2029 � March 31, 2030 Option Period 3 | 12 Months | April 1, 2030 � March 31, 2031 Option Period 4 | 12 Months | April 1, 2031 � March 31, 2032 Target Occupancy Date: April 1, 2027 (subject to adjustments based on build-out and award timelines). Estimated Cost Range / Rental Rates: Provide an estimated, non-binding rental rate range for the proposed space, expressed as a fully serviced (gross) rate per rentable square foot (RSF) per year. Please specify what utilities, janitorial services, or common area maintenance (CAM) fees are included in this estimated rate, as well as any estimated costs for Tenant Improvements (TI) required to meet the security/furniture requirements. If utilities are not included, please provide an estimated average cost per month for necessary utilities and number of people the estimate is based on 4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested property owners, brokers, or authorized representatives who can meet the above requirements are requested to submit a brief capability statement. Responses should include the following: Property Information: Address and brief description of the building. Available Space: Exact ABOA square footage available. Floor Plans/Photos: Include photos showing the current layout. Availability: Date the space will be available for occupancy or tenant improvements. Point of Contact: Name, email, and phone number of the property representative. 5. RESPONSE DEADLINE Responses must be submitted via email to Michael Dunford at michael.dunford@us.af.mil and copy AFLCMC.WVG.LookingGlass-Next@us.af.mil no later than 3:00PM on October 28, 2026. title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of IX-551
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of IX-551. The IX-551 characteristics are Length: 260 FT, Width: 85 FT, Age: 10 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 8 FT 6 IN, Full Displacement: 3,070 L Tons and Light Load: 2,267 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of IX-551 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the Asset to the Contractors facility. Upon docking the Asset, wash, and clean the exterior surfaces of the Asset. Blast and preserve all exterior hull surfaces, underwater body, freeboard, moon pools and bulwark surfaces of the Asset. Fill, drain, air test, inspect each underwater skeg on the Asset. Accomplish visual inspections of hull and body and all tank/voids. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes and hardware on the underwater hull. Shift the Asset on the blocks to achieve 100 percent preservation of underwater hull. Apply non-skid system to main deck and 02/03 level decks. Accomplish preliminary and final air tests to tanks/voids. Open, pump, ventilate, gas free and clean all tanks. Accomplish partial preservation of Qty (24 EA) tanks. Preserve tank/void manhole covers. Identify distinguishing figures and markings, Remove, clean and reinstall rubber fenders. Open and inspect all pumps and overboard discharge valves. Accomplish visual inspection and final closeout inspection of each tank/void upon completion of all work. title: Maintenance, Repair and Preservation of IX-551
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of IX-551. The IX-551 characteristics are Length: 260 FT, Width: 85 FT, Age: 10 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 8 FT 6 IN, Full Displacement: 3,070 L Tons and Light Load: 2,267 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of IX-551 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the Asset to the Contractors facility. Upon docking the Asset, wash, and clean the exterior surfaces of the Asset. Blast and preserve all exterior hull surfaces, underwater body, freeboard, moon pools and bulwark surfaces of the Asset. Fill, drain, air test, inspect each underwater skeg on the Asset. Accomplish visual inspections of hull and body and all tank/voids. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes and hardware on the underwater hull. Shift the Asset on the blocks to achieve 100 percent preservation of underwater hull. Apply non-skid system to main deck and 02/03 level decks. Accomplish preliminary and final air tests to tanks/voids. Open, pump, ventilate, gas free and clean all tanks. Accomplish partial preservation of Qty (24 EA) tanks. Preserve tank/void manhole covers. Identify distinguishing figures and markings, Remove, clean and reinstall rubber fenders. Open and inspect all pumps and overboard discharge valves. Accomplish visual inspection and final closeout inspection of each tank/void upon completion of all work. Install new manhole gaskets and fasteners. Undock the Asset. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the Asset back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by this Statement of Work or described in this Scope Overview are included in section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. title: Multiple Award IDIQ Contract for Design Build & General Construction Services - New York & New Jersey
description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION Point of contact: Belkys H. Torres Rivera; belkys.torresrivera@gsa.gov Set-Aside: The Procurement will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside. See Set Aside Requirements below. PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M 2. ACQUISITION DETAILS 2.1 Scope of Work This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) General Construction and Design-Build Construction Services Contract for Federally-Owned and Federally-Leased Space located within Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4. IDIQ Contractors will be offered the opportunity to submit proposals for general construction and design-build Task Orders under this Contract as described elsewhere in this Statement of Work (SOW) and applicable Contract documents. The Contractor shall provide professional services for the planning, design, and construction necessary to meet the requirements of the individual Task Orders. Specific requirements of individual Task Orders will be issued by Request For Proposals on a Task Order basis. Task Order services shall be provided according to the general requirements described herein, and as further described in the Task Order Request For Proposals and accompanying documents. Disciplines and expertise that may be required to accomplish the scopes of the Task Orders include, but are not limited to: architecture, engineering (Disciplines: mechanical, electrical, plumbing, civil, structural and fire protection), vertical transportation, life safety, code compliance, security, historic preservation, estimating, construction project management and building construction services. 2.2 Place of Performance The Zones 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4 are detailed below by counties. Zone 1 - Metropolitan New York City Area (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following Counties): Bronx (NY), Kings (Brooklyn, NY), New York (Manhattan, NY), Queens (NY), Richmond (Staten Island, NY), Suffolk (NY), Nassau (NY), Westchester (NY), Bergen (NJ), Essex (NJ), Hudson (NJ), Middlesex (NJ), Monmouth (NJ), Morris (NJ), Passaic (NJ) and Union (NJ). Zone 2 - Western Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie, Genesee, Livingston, Monroe, Niagara, Ontario, Orleans, Steuben, Wayne, Wyoming and Yates. Zone 3 - Central Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Broome, Cayuga, Chemung, Chenango, Cortland, Delaware, Herkimer, Jefferson, Lewis, Madison, Oneida, Onondaga, Oswego, Otsego, St. Lawrence, Schuyler, Seneca, Tioga and Tompkins. Zone 4 - Eastern Upstate New York (All Federal Buildings and Leased Locations located in the following New York Counties): Albany, Clinton, Columbia, Dutchess, Essex, Franklin, Fulton, Greene, Hamilton, Montgomery, Orange, Putnam, Rensselaer, Rockland, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Sullivan, Ulster, Warren and Washington. 2.3 Period of Performance 2.3.1 IDIQ Level This IDIQ Contract includes a one-year Base period and four (4) One-Year Options, totaling five (5) years. The Base Year will commence upon the Notice to Proceed, with Base Year services, and end one (1) calendar year from the date specified on the Notice to Proceed. At the end of the Base Year, the Government may elect to exercise the Option for Option Year 1. At the end of each Option Year, the Government may, or may not, elect to exercise the option for the following Option Year. After award, the Government will issue a written Notice to Proceed to the successful Contractors, who shall provide contractual services via issuance of individual task orders during the twelve-month Base Year period. The Five-Year Contract may be extended for up to an additional six (6) months pending award of a new (succeeding) follow-on contract (see FAR 52.217-8). It is the intent of the Government to provide for at least thirty (30) calendar days prior notice of intent to exercise this option. 2.3.2 Task Order Level Each Task Order awarded will state the period of performance and the amount of calendar days allowed to complete the referenced project. 2.4 Contract Magnitude Per Far 36.204, the magnitude of the entire requirement is more than $10,000,000.00. 2.5 Contract Type 2.5.1 IDIQ Contract: The Contract will be a Multiple Award IDIQ Contract awarded on a Firm-Fixed Priced basis that will cover four (4) geographical locations: Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4. It is anticipated that a total of approximately ten (10) Contracts will be awarded for Zone 1 and a total of approximately five (5) Contracts for each Zones 2, 3, and 4 (total of approximately fifteen (15) Contracts). A maximum of approximately twenty-five (25) Contracts will be awarded from this solicitation. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. An Offeror can submit offers for each Zone and may be awarded for one (1) or more Zones, based on its qualifications and overall ranking determined at Source Selection. 2.5.2 Task Orders: All subsequent Task Orders will be issued during the ordering period of the Contract�s period of performance. Task orders will be issued on a firm-fixed-price basis. Task orders will be competed amongst all of the awarded IDIQ Contractors on a fair opportunity basis in accordance with FAR 16.507, unless an exception is determined to be appropriate. The value of any Task Orders issued under this Contract will have an overall award value range up to $20,000,000.00. 2.6 Maximum Order Limit The Maximum Order Limit (MOL)/Contract Ceiling amount for this acquisition is $500,000,000 for the life of all awarded Multiple Award Contracts (five years) and none of the individual IDIQ Contracts will have a maximum order/annual ceiling limitation. 2.7 Set-Aside Requirement The solicitation set-aside requirements will be identified as seen below: -This Solicitation is total set-aside for Small Businesses, in accordance with FAR 19. -There will be a total of approximately ten (10) IDIQ Awards for Zone 1 and a total of approximately five (5) IDIQ awards for each of Zones 2, 3 and 4. A total of approximately twenty-five (25) IDIQ awards for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for HubZone for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for HubZones for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for Service Disabled Veterans Owned Small Businesses (SDVOB) for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for SDVOSB for the entire requirement; -There will be up to one (1) IDIQ award reserved for Women Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) for each Zone, with a total of up to four (4) IDIQ awards reserved for WOSB for the entire requirement; -Each Offeror�s socioeconomic status will be checked in the System for Award Management on sam.gov at the time of proposal submission and at award for validation purposes in addition to providing any requested supporting documentation for its socioeconomic status requested in the solicitation. An offer will not be evaluated or considered for award if it fails to meet the Small Business size status requirements under NAICS Code 236220- Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; -An Offeror may submit a proposal for each Zone for award consideration; -In the event that there is an insufficient number of acceptable Offers with fair and reasonable price from a particular socioeconomic category, then the remaining numbers of IDIQ awards shall go to a Small Business concern. 2.8 Bonding Requirements 2.8.1 IDIQ Level: Bid guarantees, performance, and payment bonds are not required at proposal submission on the IDIQ level. title: J--Sources Sought Notice
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. Responses will be used for market research to determine appropriate acquisition strategies. No reimbursement will be provided for responding. Any future solicitation will be posted separately on SAM.gov, and interested parties are responsible for monitoring that site. 1. Purpose: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) is conducting market research to identify qualified small businesses�including Small Business, Veteran-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone, Small Disadvantaged, Women-Owned, Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises, and 8(a) firms�capable of providing deployment, maintenance, operation, repair, and technical support services for the Albuquerque Seismological Laboratory (ASL). 2. Background: ASL operates more than 330 seismograph stations worldwide, including approximately 230 in the continental United States. ASL installs, operates, and maintains the USGS component of the Global Seismographic Network (GSN) and the Advanced National Seismic System (ANSS). These networks support: a. Real-time earthquake monitoring (USGS NEIC) b. Tsunami warning operations (NOAA) c. Nuclear test monitoring (CTBTO and U.S. Air Force) d. International scientific research communities 3. Scope of Requirement: The anticipated requirement includes but is not limited to: a. Deployment, installation, maintenance, operation, modification, and repair of domestic and international seismological instrument systems b. Collection and processing of digital and analog seismic data c. Facilities, engineering, and technical support services Example labor categories include: Field Engineering Manager, Senior Field Engineer, Field Engineer, Electronic Technician, Electronic/Mechanical Facilities Technician, and Permitting Specialist (regional network support). Contractor tasks may include inspections, adjustments, part replacement, testing, minor repairs, monitoring, setup, cable fabrication, and related technical activities. Work requires applied electronics knowledge and use of common test instruments (e.g., multimeters, audio generators, oscilloscopes). Typical equipment includes: Quanterra Q330HR, Kinemetrics Slate, Quanterra Baler, Streckeisen STS 1/STS 2/STS 2.5, Geotech KS54000, Nanometrics Trillium 240/120, G�ralp CMG 3T/3TB, Kinemetrics FBA23, and Episensor accelerometers. 4. Period of Performance: One (1) twelve month base period and four (4) twelve month option periods. 5. NAICS Code: NAICS 811210 - Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance. Size standard: $30M 6. SAM Registration: All interested firms must be registered in SAM.gov to be eligible for a future award. Registration information is available at: https://www.sam.gov. 7. Requested Information: Interested small businesses shall submit a capabilities package addressing the following: 1. Professional Qualifications: a. Relevant professional registrations, education, certifications, and training b. Qualifications of key personnel (prime and subcontractors) c. Staffing capacity to support multiple, simultaneous technical tasks 2. Capability & Technical Experience: a. Demonstrated experience relevant to seismological operations, maintenance, and equipment repair b. Description of technical competencies aligned with ASL mission needs 3. Specialized Experience: a. Breadth and diversity of past projects b. Demonstrated use of technologies required for seismic network operations c. Resumes for proposed personnel showing direct fieldwork and instrumentation experience 4. Past Performance: (within the last 4 years) a. Government or commercial past performance b. Cost control, quality of work, schedule compliance c. Customer satisfaction and working relationship quality Include your UEI number and ensure all small business representations are current in SAM.gov. 8. Additional Professional Support: Additional services may be required on an as needed basis (e.g., Russian Translator; may be integrated with other positions). 9. Submission Instructions: Provide a capabilities package addressing all above elements to Mary Beth Wilson at beth_wilson@ios.doi.gov. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice are not adequate responses to any future solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be announced separately on SAM.gov.

title: NATO Business Opportunity: Integration and Commissioning of the RACCOON Initial Capability
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for the integration and commissioning of the initial instance of a CIS capability codenamed RACCOON. RACCOON is intended to provide highly available and resilient data services, including communications and collaboration, as well as virtual desktop infrastructure for end users. To bid on this contract, potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 3) hold a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the level of SECRET or higher, 4) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 5) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement The reference for the solicitation is NCP-CO-424385-RACCOON and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT Objective: RACCOON will implement a private cloud, consisting of one management domain and two workload domains, isolated from each other, and operating at the same security classification level, using Broadcom VMWare Cloud Foundation (VCF). This private cloud will evolve over time, in terms of number of nodes. These nodes will be operated as a VCF fleet, hereafter referred to as the RACCOON cluster. This initial RACCOON cluster will be limited to two (2) nodes (as the first two VCF instances in the VCF fleet). It will deliver the foundational capability for the provision of services to a number of endpoints. The provision of these endpoints, with quantities also evolving over time, will be covered under other follow-on projects under the same overarching program. Scope: Together with the first two (2) nodes of the RACCOON cluster, the scope includes one (1) Reference, Testing and Validation (RTV) node, and one (1) Service Operating Centre (SOC) and its associated Cybersecurity Operating Centre (CSOC). The latter will constitute an endpoint on its own, including end user devices (EUD) for the administrators of the capability. The RTV will be a scaled-down RACCOON node to support testing and verification activities during implementation and during operation. The capability will be implemented in accordance with an existing High Level Design (HLD), which is derived from an interim CIS Design and Security Architecture (iCDSA). The iCDSA forms the basis for Security Accreditation. The supporting hardware, software, and bearer networks specified in the HLD are currently in procurement and, alongside the HLD document itself, will be provided to the successful Bidder as Purchaser-Furnished Items (PFI). The physical rooms at static facilities and/or relocatable shelters, intended to host the RACCOON nodes, the RTV Node and the SOC/CSOC endpoint, will also be provided as PFI. They will be provided with all the power, cooling, rack space, desk space and associated furniture, and physical security required for the integration. A detailed description of them will also be provided to the successful Bidder as PFI. Site Surveys will be conducted following Contract Award, as required. The scope of the works in this procurement includes, but it is not limited to: 1) the production of the low-level design (LLD) based on the PFI; 2) the physical and logical integration and configuration of the initial RACCOON cluster, the RTV, and the SOC and CSOC, as a fully functional system; 3) the system commissioning activities, i.e. testing and verification, security accreditation, and operational acceptance. In terms of cybersecurity, the scope includes, but it is not limited to, the integration and commissioning of endpoint protection, firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems and data guards, as well as other cybersecurity modules developed by external contracts, in particular, but not limited to, PKI, Logs Aggregation and On-line Vulnerability Assessment; and cryptographic equipment, all as PFI. The Core Nodes, the RTV node and the SOC/CSOC endpoint will be located in different NATO Nations� territory in Europe. Key Deliverables: The key deliverables of this procurement are: � The first two (2) nodes of the RACCOON cluster, integrated and operational; � One (1) RTV node, integrated and operational; � One (1) SOC and CSOC endpoint, integrated and operational; � All the Technical Management and Engineering efforts required for the successful integration and commissioning of the above; � All the associated documentation, e.g. the Low Level Design (LLD) and the As-Built documentation, ILS documentation, etc; � All the required Project Management efforts for the successful integration and commissioning to occur in the contractual time, cost and scope; � All the required Quality Assurance Management efforts to guarantee the highest quality standards in the delivered capability. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. The U.S. Government continues to accept the legacy NATO International Competitive Bidding (ICB) application for participation in NCP. U.S. firms can download a copy of the legacy ICB application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the TEXT of your email: - the title and/or solicitation number of the project - the name/phone/email of the company employee who should receive the bid documents After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the project. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency.
